findings.message: `ref_verify_run`, `ref_verify_check_approved`, and `ref_verify_results` execute application flow by calling `RefVerifyDriver::handle` and returning its `CommandOutcome`. Composition must stop at `ref_verify_driver`; the CLI layer should invoke the returned driver.

`track_type_signals` invokes `TypeSignalsInteractor::run` and converts its result into a command outcome. Move request execution to `cli_driver`; this root should only construct and return the wired primary adapter.
`track_type_graph` constructs a user-facing command-removal message inside the composition root. Deprecation rendering belongs in `cli_driver`, with composition limited to wiring.

`track_baseline_graph` invokes `RenderBaselineGraph::execute` and then formats the user-facing success message. Both execution and rendering must be handled by a wired primary adapter in `cli_driver`.
`track_contract_map` calls `ContractMapDriver::handle` from the composition entry point. Return the fully wired driver instead and let `apps/cli` invoke it.

`track_catalogue_spec_signals` implements the application workflow in composition: it validates filesystem state, selects layers, deletes stale artifacts, and invokes `refresh_one_layer`. Move this orchestration behind a use-case/driver boundary and retain only collaborator construction here.
`track_spec_element_hash` directly invokes the infrastructure hash operation and serializes its result for display. Execution and JSON rendering belong behind a `cli_driver` primary adapter.
`track_baseline_capture` invokes `BaselineCaptureInteractor::run` from the composition root. Expose a wired driver and perform the request invocation in `apps/cli`.
`track_lint` invokes `RunCatalogueLint::execute` and formats violations, counts, and user-facing errors locally. Move execution and presentation into `cli_driver`, leaving this method as pure wiring.

`track_catalogue_impl_signals` invokes `CatalogueImplSignalsInteractor::run` and maps its report into CLI output. The composition root must instead return a wired primary adapter without executing it.

T001 description restates upstream behavior (ordering, filtering, persistence, gate judgment, and rendering) instead of limiting the plan text to target + operation + anchors. See `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

T002 description restates the source derivation, artifact-reading, validation, and non-persistence contract in prose. Keep those requirements in the cited spec elements and retain only target + operation + anchors here. See `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.
T003 description restates the output completeness and failure-rendering behavior in prose beyond the executable target/operation/anchor form. See `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

T004 description restates the unchanged-command/routes behavior contract (`sotp track resolve` and existing Signal routes) instead of relying on its anchors. See `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

Section S2 restates upstream behavior by requiring persisted artifacts/evaluators to be connected and derived results not to be saved. Keep the section as target + operation + anchor cite; cite `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

Section S4 restates the upstream non-target-command behavior contract by requiring existing Signal dispatch behavior to be preserved. Keep the section as target + operation + anchor cite; cite `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

T001 includes upstream behavior prose: “The usecase selects and returns occurrences without runtime I/O.” Retain only target, operation, and anchor cites; see `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.
T002 restates the upstream source-selection, derivation, evaluation-rule, and persistence contract in prose. See `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.
T003 restates the upstream occurrence-output contract by listing every rendered field. See `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.
T004 restates the upstream `track resolve` behavior-preservation contract. See `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.
Section S2 restates the upstream in-memory derivation behavior for chains without persisted artifacts. See `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.
Section S4 restates the upstream requirement that `track resolve` remain unchanged. See `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

AC-05 and OUT-01 are mapped only to T004, but T004 neither targets `sotp track resolve` nor specifies a regression-validation step. Adding the separate report command and its wiring cannot itself verify that resolve output remains unchanged. Add an explicit regression test operation to T004 or a dedicated validation task.

T003 bundles two independently verifiable behavior units: filter-to-query conversion (IN-03/AC-03) and occurrence rendering (IN-02/AC-02). Its contract entries already separate the filter/input DTOs from `SignalReportDriver`; split these units into ordered tasks and update their coverage, attribution, estimates, and batches.

T004 bundles independently verifiable work across two scopes: CLI parsing/dispatch (IN-01, IN-03, AC-01, AC-03) and composition-root wiring (CN-01, AC-04). Split composition wiring from the CLI transport task, with an explicit dependency, and place AC-05 regression validation in the appropriate CLI/validation task.

T004 implements `SignalReportDriver`, but its `depends_on` lists only T001 even though T003 creates the `SignalReportInput` and filter DTOs consumed by that driver. Add T003 as a dependency or reorder/split the tasks so T004 does not refer to artifacts not yet created.

T005 adds CLI dispatch before T006 creates `SignalCompositionRoot::signal_report_driver`, which the dispatch must obtain to invoke the report path. The declared order B3 (T005) → B4 (T006) is therefore not independently implementable; composition-root wiring must precede the dispatch task or the dependency direction must be redesigned.

B2 contains both producer T003 and consumer T004 even though T004 explicitly declares `depends_on: ["T001", "T003"]`. This allows occurrence-rendering work to begin before T003’s filter/input types are verifiably complete. Move T004 to a later batch and keep T006/T005 after it.

T001 claims the `SignalReportInteractor` behavior, but T002 is ordered after it and owns creation of `SignalReportSourcePort::load`. The type catalogue defines `SignalReportInteractor::new(Arc<dyn SignalReportSourcePort>)`, so T001 cannot be independently implemented and verified before that port exists. Keep the port contract with T001 and make the infrastructure adapter depend on it, or redesign the dependency boundary.

T002's justification—“separating their contract and non-persistence proof would leave neither task independently implementable”—is implausible. The usecase port can be verified with the interactor/mock contract, while the infrastructure adapter has its own conformance and non-persistence tests. These are independently verifiable units under IN-04/CN-01/AC-04 and should be split before T002 starts.

T002's description and task-contract attribution touch both the usecase `SignalReportSourcePort` and infrastructure adapter, but its estimate declares only the infrastructure scope. B2 therefore omits a touched scope from its per-scope estimate sum, making its ceiling composition unsound. Add the usecase estimate or correct the task split and attribution.

Batch B1 groups T001 and T002 even though T002 declares `depends_on: ["T001"]` and its description begins “After T001”. This allows the consumer task to be scheduled in the same batch as its producer, violating the required ordered completion boundary; place T002 in a later batch.

T002 now claims to “repair its shared canonical TDDD loader”, but `task-contract.json` attributes T002 only to `SystemSignalReportSourceAdapter`. The loader repair is an additional claimed modification with no corresponding catalogue-entry attribution, so the task contract is incomplete.

T005 is still `todo` but bundles two independently verifiable behavior units: signal-report parsing/dispatch (IN-01, IN-03, AC-01, AC-03) and the separate `sotp track resolve` non-regression check (OUT-01, AC-05). Split these into separate tasks before implementation starts, preserving the current dependencies for the command task and assigning the regression task its own explicit dependency.

T007 names the user-facing `sotp track resolve` command but no source/test file or implementation symbol, so the executor must invent where this regression validation belongs. Add a concrete target such as the relevant `apps/cli/` test module while retaining OUT-01 and AC-05.

T007 and section S4 restate AC-05's behavior in prose (“display and behavior remain unchanged”) instead of using target + operation + anchor cites. Replace that clause in both places with a short operation such as `sotp track resolve` regression validation plus OUT-01 / AC-05, as required by `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

`context()` uses ambient `SystemGitRepo::discover()`, so `GIT_DIR`/related Git environment variables can redirect the report to a different repository than the current working tree. The adapter should use isolated repository discovery and verify the resulting root before reading artifacts.

The adapter performs unbounded filesystem reads via `read_to_string` (and delegates ADR reads to an also-unbounded filesystem adapter) for user-controlled repository artifacts. A very large artifact can exhaust memory; enforce the repository's bounded-read policy before decoding.

`context()` uses ambient `SystemGitRepo::discover()`, so `GIT_DIR` and related Git environment variables can redirect the report to a different repository than the current working tree. Use isolated repository discovery and verify the resulting root before reading artifacts.

`read_text()` uses unbounded `std::fs::read_to_string` for repository-controlled artifacts, and ADR loading delegates to another unbounded filesystem read. A very large artifact can exhaust memory; enforce a bounded-read limit before decoding.

The catalog-spec and impl-catalog paths call `tddd_layers::load_tddd_layers`, whose architecture-rules loader still uses unbounded `read_to_string`. A repository-controlled oversized `architecture-rules.json` can exhaust memory before the adapter returns its typed error; apply the bounded-read policy to this input path.

`context()` isolates repository discovery, but `repo.current_branch()` is not isolated: `SystemGitRepo::current_branch()` invokes the ambient Git environment through `output()`. `GIT_DIR`/related variables can therefore supply a branch from another repository, causing this adapter to read the wrong track artifacts from the discovered workspace. Branch resolution must use the same repository-selection isolation.

`reject_symlinks_below` does not verify that `path` is beneath `trusted_root`; when the two paths are unrelated it simply walks to the filesystem root and accepts a regular file. Consequently both public loaders can read an attacker-selected `architecture-rules.json` outside the trusted workspace. Apply the fail-closed containment validation used by the `is_safe_briefing_path`/guarded-reader patterns before opening the file, including canonical containment after resolution.

A missing `architecture-rules.json` is converted to an empty workspace-crate set, and the parser also defaults a missing `layers` field to empty. This silently disables the gate-relevant IN-10 reverse checks. Fail closed as `load_tddd_layers` does instead of treating absent configuration as a valid default.

The catalogue-spec report iterates every TDDD-enabled binding without checking `catalogue_spec_signal_enabled()`. A legitimate configuration with this signal disabled for one layer has no corresponding artifact, so that layer makes the entire `CatalogSpec` report fail even when other enabled layers are reportable. Filter bindings using the same activation check as the canonical signal calculation/check paths.

A missing impl-catalog signal artifact is silently skipped because `None` continues the loop. This makes an unavailable layer indistinguishable from an all-blue layer and returns a successful but incomplete report. Missing artifacts for expected TDDD-enabled layers must fail closed with `SourceUnavailable(ImplCatalog)`.

`context()` maps every discovery, branch, and track-id failure to `SourceUnavailable(AdrUser)`, and `load()` propagates that unchanged for all requested chains. Thus a `CatalogSpec`, `SpecAdr`, or `ImplCatalog` query reports the wrong failed chain, violating the port's selected-chain error contract. Map context failures to the chain passed to `load`.

The ADR report path enumerates and accumulates every ADR without a file-count or aggregate-byte bound. Per-file bounded reads do not prevent a repository containing an unbounded number of ADR files from exhausting memory or runtime. Enforce a total input/count ceiling and return a typed source error when exceeded.

`confined_rules_path` canonicalizes `trusted_root` before checking whether it or an ancestor is a symlink. That erases the symlink evidence: supplying a symlinked root together with a target-resolved rules path makes containment and the later guard pass, because `reject_symlinks_below` excludes the canonical root itself. Reject symlinked root components before canonicalization, following the real-root policy used by `scope_config_loader`/`ensure_not_symlink_root`.

The architecture-rules DTOs omit the top-level `version` and lack `deny_unknown_fields`, so unsupported versions and misspelled TDDD fields are silently accepted and interpreted with defaults. For example, a typo in `catalogue_spec_signal.enabled` disables that gate without a parse error. Parse and reject unsupported versions first, then strictly deserialize the consumed configuration blocks as in the `agent_profiles` codec pattern.

`parse_workspace_crate_names` still accepts `{"layers":[]}` and returns an empty set. Because this set enables the gate-relevant IN-10 reverse checks, an empty configuration silently disables those checks. Reject an empty array consistently with `parse_tddd_layers` rather than treating it as valid configuration.

The new count ceiling is applied only after `FsAdrFileAdapter::list_adr_paths()` has already read the entire directory into an unbounded `Vec`. A repository with an excessive number of ADR entries can therefore exhaust time or memory before `MAX_ADR_FILES` is checked. Enforce the ceiling while enumerating entries and fail immediately when it is exceeded.

`read_impl_catalog` uses `FsImplCatalogSignalReader`, which hardcodes `<layer>-type-signals.json`, while the canonical calculator writes `binding.signal_file()` derived from the configured `catalogue_file`. With a supported custom catalogue filename, the report rejects an existing signal artifact and also constructs the wrong catalogue reference at line 281. Resolve the artifact with `binding.signal_file()` and reference `binding.catalogue_file()`.

`read_impl_catalog()` now treats every configured layer's implementation-signal file as mandatory. The previous port path used `read_optional_signals()` and skipped absent artifacts; with a normal track whose signals have not yet been generated, `SignalReportSourcePort::load(ImplCatalog)` now fails the entire report instead of returning the available occurrences. Preserve optional-file semantics while still rejecting malformed or unsafe files.

`read_impl_catalog()` still treats every configured layer's implementation-signal file as mandatory. The previous adapter path used `read_optional_signals()` and skipped absent artifacts; on a normal track before signals are generated, `SignalReportSourcePort::load(ImplCatalog)` now fails the whole report instead of returning available occurrences. Preserve optional-file semantics while continuing to reject malformed or unsafe existing files.

`MAX_ADR_FILES` only limits matching Markdown files after filtering, so `bounded_adr_paths` still performs an unbounded `read_dir` walk over non-Markdown files, directories, and other entries. A repository with many junk entries can therefore force unbounded I/O despite the advertised enumeration ceiling. Count every directory entry examined and fail once the ceiling is exceeded.

Mirror-chain divergence: cli_driver::SignalReportLevelFilter is documented as mapping exhaustively into usecase::SignalReportLevelSelection, but its variants are Yellow/Red/YellowAndRed while the usecase selection uses YellowOnly/RedOnly/YellowAndRed. No documented language-level reason explains the renamed variants, so the conversion mirror is not structurally aligned.

The docs for infrastructure::SystemSignalReportSourceAdapter and usecase::SignalReportSourcePort restate the upstream derivation, persistence, filtering, and read-only behavior contracts in prose instead of only naming the changed surface and citing IN-04/CN-01/AC-04. This violates the no-upstream-restatement policy.

Multiple CLI, composition, driver, and usecase entries restate upstream command behavior, defaults, conversion, rendering, CQRS, and validation contracts in their docs rather than using anchor-only references. Affected entries include cli::SignalReportArgs, cli::SignalReportChainArg, cli::SignalReportOnlyArg, cli_composition::SignalCompositionRoot, cli_driver::SignalReportChainFilter, cli_driver::SignalReportDriver, cli_driver::SignalReportInput, cli_driver::SignalReportLevelFilter, usecase::SignalReportService, usecase::SignalReportInteractor, and the SignalReport* value-object/report DTO entries.

Mirror-chain field divergence: cli::SignalReportArgs declares the level selector as `only`, cli_driver::SignalReportInput declares it as `level`, and usecase::SignalReportQuery declares it as `levels`. These are parallel conversion payloads, but the catalogues provide no documented language-level constraint or explicit mapping rationale for the inconsistent field names.

`usecase::SignalReportSourcePort::load` is synchronous despite loading persisted signal artifacts and canonical input files, but the entry docs do not acknowledge the blocking execution choice. Document the intentional synchronous CLI boundary or make the port asynchronous.

Upstream-restatement remains in usecase::SignalReportService, usecase::SignalReportInteractor, and usecase::SignalReportQuery: their docs repeat the CQRS rationale that the collaborator/read model/error surface differs from the existing command path and that no consistency boundary is shared. Per `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`, these entries should cite GO-01/AC-01/IN-03/AC-03 without restating the upstream design rationale.

D1 requires `adr_user` to be included while forbidding signal recalculation and limiting the view to persisted `calc-*` artifacts. Chain ⓪'s `calc-adr-user` performs a live scan and persists no signal document, so the command cannot enumerate all four chains under the recorded boundary. This incompatibility must be resolved before downstream behavior can be derived.
findings.category: inconsistent decisions within the same ADR
